Events of Warcraft 1, 2, and 3

Dragonflight
Origins of the universe
The universe is created from the clash of the Light and the Void
The rise of demons
Demons arise in the Twisting Nether
The Jailer is banished to the Maw by the other Eternal Ones, and the Arbiter is created.
Banishment of the jailer
Sire Denathrius pretends to exile the nathrezim from Revendreth.
Exile of the nathrezim
Sargeras betrays the Pantheon and creates the Burning Legion.
Betrayal of Sargeras
The coming of the Old Gods
The Old Gods arrive on Azeroth
The titans find Azeroth and create the titan-forged to combat the Old Gods
Wrath of the titan-forged
Life is seeded on Azeroth by the keepers
The Ordering of Azeroth
The keepers create the Dragon Aspects
Charge of the Dragonflights
Earliest known date
The creation of the contents of Mosh'Ogg Bounty, determined through the use of a carbon-dating potion, and believed to be of Old God origin.
Rise of the eredars
The eredar race arises on the world of Argus.

The Primal Incarnates lead the Primalists rebellion against the Dragon Aspects. 

The war ends with the Primal Incarnates being sealed away; Raszageth on the Forbidden Reach and the rest in the Vault of the Incarnates.
War of the Incarnates
The dracthyr are placed into stasis in the Forbidden Reach.
Sleep of the dracthyrs
Rise of the trolls

The trolls arise on primordial Kalimdor and establish their civilization, later forming the Empire of Zul to combat the aqir in the Aqir and Troll War.

The loa Sethraliss defeats the C'Thrax Mythrax at the cost of her own life. Her sethrak followers Sulthis, Vorrik, and Korthek seal Mythrax away beneath Atul'Aman.

The war ends with the defeat of the empire of Azj'Aqir, with the surviving aqir fleeing to form the colonies of Ahn'Qiraj, Azjol-Nerub and Manti'vess.

The Amani establish the city of Zul'Aman atop the site where they have slain the C'Thrax Kith'ix.
The curse of flesh

The Curse of Flesh spreads around Azeroth :
- the Dragonflayer vrykul, see their offspring (whose descendants would later become known as humans) born stunted and weak.
- the mogu, break apart into warrior clans and begin fighting amongst themselves in the Age of a Hundred Kings.
Rise of Lei Shen

While several new races — the hozen, jinyu and pandaren — settle in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms, the mogu Lei Shen seizes power from Ra and founds the mogu empire, enslaving the other races in the region.
Rise of the night elves

A tribe of dark trolls gradually migrate towards the heart of ancient Kalimdor and settle along the shores of the Well of Eternity. Over generations, the arcane energies emanating from the Well transform them into a new race of highly intelligent beings, who call themselves "kaldorei" ("Children of the Stars") or night elves.

The kaldorei begin to actively study and practice arcane magic. They bend magic to their will and use it to build beautiful cities, craft artifacts and reshape the land. Some kaldorei resist the lure to use the Well of Eternity's power and warn others of the dangers of abusing it. Their warnings go unheeded.

A group of upper-class kaldorei begin to refer to themselves as the Highborne and revel in the use of magic.
Sargeras and the eredars

Sargeras corrupts most of the eredar on Argus, convincing them to join his Burning Legion.

With the help of the naaru, Velen escapes on the Genedar with other eredar that reject Sargeras' offer. The naaru name them the draenei, or "Exiled Ones".
War of Uldum

Lei Shen attempts to invade Uldum and seize the Forge of Origination for his empire, but is killed when Uldum's tol'vir guardians activate the Forge's destructive power. In the process, Uldum's lush jungles are scorched into a harsh desert. Lei Shen is followed by a succession of various mogu emperors.
The Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas is founded in Feralas by the Shen'dralar.
Foundation of Eldre'Thalas
Revolution pf the pandaren
Kang incites a slave revolution against the mogu, successfully overthrowing them and leading to the founding of the Pandaren Empire.

The Zandalari trolls, allies of the now-overthrown mogu, attempt to conquer a plot of land in Pandaria promised to them by Lei Shen. The invasion is repelled thanks to Jiang and the newly-founded Order of the Cloud Serpent.
The Zandalari Wars
The War of the Ancients and The Sundering

Sargeras senses the Highborne's use of the Well of Eternity and decides to invade Azeroth. Corrupting Queen Azshara and her followers, a portal is opened through which the Burning Legion enters the world and lays waste to the night-elven civilization.

Emperor Shaohao, the last emperor of the Pandaren Empire, is told of the impending invasion by a jinyu waterspeaker. After purging himself of his emotional burdens, he becomes one with the land and isolates Pandaria behind a veil of thick mists, which protects it from the war and ensuing disasters but also keeps it hidden from the rest of the world for millennia.

The Sundering of the World

Several night elves led by Malfurion Stormrage are able to destroy the Well of Eternity, preventing Sargeras from entering the world, and stopping the Legion's invasion. However, this also creates a massive cataclysm known as the Sundering, where eighty percent of Kalimdor's landmass is plunged between the waves, leaving only a handful of isolated continents.

The Dragon Isles are sealed away from the world.

In the aftermath of the war Illidan Stormrage poured a vial of the Well of Eternity water in mount Hyjal lake creating a new Well of Eternity.
Realizing what his brother has done, Malfurion imprisonned Illidan and call upon the dragon Aspects.
The elves planted the great tree Nordrasil as Ysera, Nozdormu and Alexstrasza blessed it to keep others from abusing the magic of the new Well, but also to prevent the second fount’s power from growing too great over time.
First Lunar Festival
After the War of The Ancients, the Lunar Festival is created as a time of celebration of the alliance of races against the Burning Legion.
New era of the Night Elves

After abandoning arcane magic and embrassing druidism, the burgeoning night elf society expands into the dense forests of Ashenvale. 
Malfurion Stormrage begins to train other druids.

Tyrande Whisperwind positions the Sisterhood of Elune as the leaders of the night elf government and military. 

The Sentinels are created to protect their emergent society.
War of the Satyr

Xalan the Feared rallied the Satyrs and with the help of remaining forces of the Burning Legion they wreak havoc upon the Night Elves.

With a heavy toll for the Night Elves the Satyrs were pushed back and scattered around the world with no left leadership, forcing them to live hidden in sall groups up until now.
Exile of the High Elves

Many of the surviving Highbornes grew restless of the ban on arcane magic.
Dath'Remar and his followers unleashed a magical storm upon Ashenvale wich forced the druids to act and exile them.

Dath'Remar and his followers seized this oportunity, renaimed themselves Quel'dorei and, aboard specialy crafted ships, sailed to a far away land they named Quel'Thalas where the build the High Elves society around the Sunwell creating with a vial of water from the Well of Eternity.
The Catastrophe of Moonsong Forest
The elves of Shandaral in Northrend unleash a disastrous spell during their fight against the blue dragonflight, cursing Moonsong Forest and turning it into Crystalsong Forest.
The cursed world tree

Without permission from the Cenarion Circle, Fandral Staghelm plants branches from Nordrassil in Duskwood, Hinterlands, Feralas, Crystalsong Forest, Ashenvale, and the last one in Grizzly Hills in order to stop saronite from spreading.

The Grizzly Hills sapling quickly grows into Andrassil but is corrupted by Yogg-Saron. 
The druids are forced to fell the mighty tree, which is then renamed Vordrassil.
Rescue of the Frostsaber Queen

Tyrande Whisperwind saves the frostsaber queen, Shy-Rotam, from the frostmaul giants. 

Following the event the frostsabers become allies of the night elves.
The Curse of the Mechagnomes
The Curse of Flesh affects the mechagnomes of Uldaman, turning them into gnomes. They leave Uldaman for Dun Morogh, and forget their heritage.
Rise of the Apexis
On Draenor, the arakkoa travel from Gorgrond to Arak. They create the Apexis civilization in their goddess Rukhmar's memory and begin to explore the world.
Sealing of the Barrow Deeps
The Barrow Deeps of Mount Hyjal are sealed shut.
The Founding of Arathor and the Troll Wars

After a 6 year long tribal war, the human tribes in the northern lands of the Eastern Kingdoms unite and form the kingdom of Arathor and found the city-state of Strom as their capital. 

Under the leadership of king Thoradin they lend their help to the high elves of Quel'Thalas, and together they defeat the Amani trolls. 
In return for their help, the elves start teaching arcane magic to humans.
The Expansion of Arathor
The kingdom of Arathor expands, founding settlements in Alterac, Tirisfal Glades, Gilneas, Kul Tiras, and Dalaran the city of Mages.
The guardians of Tirisfal

The reckless use of magic by humans draws the attention of demons from the Burning Legion, and they start manifesting in Azeroth. 
Mages from Dalaran form the Council of Tirisfal to secretly fight and contain the demons, without alerting the general population.
The first Guardian

The Council of Tirisfal finds a way to empower a champion permanently with their powers, in order to fight threats that the Council can't handle by themselves. 
Thus the office of the Guardian of Tirisfal is created, with Alodi becoming the first Guardian. 
Each new Guardian takes the mantle for a hundred years, before passing their powers to an apprentice.
Awakening of the Dwarves

After being afflected with the Curse of the Flesh, the earthen of Uldaman awaken with the memories of their past.
The began migrating west, founding Khaz Modan. 
They establish the city of Ironforge and assist the nearby gnomes in founding Gnomeregan.
The destruction of the Evergrowth

On Draenor, Gnarlgar rallies the Primals against the Apexis and creates a new Sporemound known as Taala. 
The Apexis annihilate the Primal army with the Breath of Rukhmar, permanently destroying the Evergrowth and preventing it from ever returning again, leading to a golden age of mortal civilization on Draenor.
The Gurubashi civil war

The Atal'ai Hakkari, followers of the loa Hakkar, and the rest of the Gurubashi fought as the result of the high cost of sacrifices to Hakkar the Soulflayer. 
With help from the Zandalari, the Atal'ai fanatics are defeated and banished from Stranglethorn Vale and they settled in the nearby Swamp of Sorrows, where they began construction of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar.
The Seven Kingdoms

The human kingdoms of Lordaeron, Alterac, Gilneas, Dalaran, and Stromgarde are formed on continental Lordaeron, north of Khaz Modan. 
The kingdom of Stormwind (also known as Azeroth) is formed on continental Azeroth. 
The kingdom of Kul Tiras is formed off of the coast of Khaz Modan.
The Betrayal of Tortheldrin

After living hidden in Eldre'Thalas since the Sundering, Tortheldrin and his followers killed most of their Shen'dralar elven kin in order to hoard the demon Immol'thar's power for themselves. 
Most of the city is abandoned, and other creatures start moving in. 
While many Shen'dralar escaped into remote regions of Kalimdor or went into hiding, those still within the dying city continued to feed and grew ever dependent on their fel addiction.
The Apexis civil war
The Apexis civilization is destroyed in a civil war. The Breath of Rukhmar explodes, shattering Arak's single spire into numerous smaller ones.
The Awakening of Theradras

The tauren inadvertently awaken the slumbering Princess Theradras, who drains the fertile lands of Mashan'she of energy, turning the region into a barren plain later called Desolace. Zaetar arrives to investigate but falls in love with Theradras, and from their union the centaur are born. After killing their father, the centaur proliferate across Desolace and begin hunting down the tauren, igniting a long and bloody war between the two races. Maraudon, the site of Zaetar's tomb, becomes treated as holy ground by the centaur.
The Ogre Rebellion

The ogres are taught arcane magic by the arakkoa and rebel against their ogron masters under the leadership of Gog Gronnslayer. The city of Goria is established, beginning the reign of the Gorian Empire.
The sleep of Malfurion
Malfurion Stormrage meets with Tyrande Whisperwind for the last time until the Third War before going entering his sleep and joining the Emerald Dream
The War of the Shifting Sands

C'Thun and the qiraji awaken and attack Kalimdor. Fandral Staghelm leads night elves and dragons against the qiraji, pushing them back to the desert of Silithus. They are successful in sealing them within Ahn'Qiraj, but Fandral's son Valstann is slain in battle.
Aegwynn and the Dragon Hunt

Aegwynn, Guardian of Tirisfal, battles and defeats an avatar of Sargeras in the Dragonblight. 
She buries the remains of the avatar in the Tomb of Sargeras in the sunken ruins of Suramar. Sargeras' spirit, however, hides itself inside Aegwynn.
The journey of the Great Turtle

Liu Lang defies Pandaria's belief that the rest of the world had been destroyed in the Sundering, and travels through the mists on the turtle Shen-zin Su. 
He returns every five years to bring more people along with him. Shen-zin Su grows large enough to become the Wandering Isle, with pandaren creating permanent settlements on his back.

The orcs emerge from the subterranean caverns of Gorgrond and begin to spread across Draenor, forming various clans.

Orcs from the Shadowmoon clan are taught the ways of shamanism by the elements and construct a temple at a site they name the Throne of the Elements. The biannual Kosh'harg festival is established.
The Emergence of the Orcs

Aegwynn decides to stay as the Guardian of Tirisfal indefinitely, partly due to her concerns about the Council of Tirisfal meddling with the politics of different nations, and partly due to Sargeras' influence. 
She builds Karazhan as her secret abode, but after the Tirisgarde find her, she moves to the Guardian Sanctum in sunken Suramar.
The Choice of Aegwynn

Pridelord Karash of the Bloodmane saberon declares war upon the high arakkoa but is defeated by the Talon King Terokk. 
Terokk establishes the city of Skyreach but is later betrayed by the Anhari priesthood, who wish to retain sole control over arakkoan society. 
Terokk and his daughter Lithic are thrown into the Sethekk Hollow to become Outcasts. Lithic dies in the fall, but Terokk and his followers are guided by Anzu to create the talonpriests and establish the city of Skettis. 
Terokk eventually becomes insane and is sealed in a realm of shadow by his followers.
War of the Arakoa
The high elven Farstriders are officially formed.
Foundation of the Farstriders
Queen Azshara imprisons the kraken Leviroth in the waters of the Riplash Ruins and blesses the trident of Riplash's emperor Raj Naz'jan so it can slay the monster if it ever escapes.
The Fall of Leviroth

Imperator Molok of the Gorian Empire sends an ogre army to claim the Throne of the Elements and the power of the elements by force. The dissonance between the ogres' reckless arcane magic and the lingering power of Grond's remains creates an explosion that blows apart the orcish temple, leaving behind only a few standing stones and throwing the elements into disarray across Draenor.
Explosion of the Throne of the Elements
Union of the Clans
At the Kosh'harg festival, the orcish clans band together to combat the ogres at the urging of Nelgarm.
Siege of Goria

The orcs lay siege to the ogre capital Goria. Molok and his sorcerers create the red pox, which begins to spread among the orcs, but Nelgarm and his fellow shaman convince the elements to completely destroy Goria.
The quest of King Mechagon
The last gnome king, King Mechagon, leads his followers in search of a mystical land of technology.
The last Genesaur
Last reported case of a genesaur birth on Draenor prior to the creation of the Blooming Genesaur.
Founding of the Earthen Ring
A group of tauren founded the order of the Earthen Ring to lead their people with wisdom and maintain the harmony between the elemental spirits.
The War of the Three Hammers

In the mountain peaks of Khaz Modan, the dwarven High King Modimus Anvilmar dies, and civil war erupts among the the Bronzebeard, Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans. The Bronzebeard clan emerges as the victor and takes control of the dwarves' capital city of Ironforge; the Wildhammers relocate to Grim Batol, while the Dark Irons become enslaved by Ragnaros under the newly-created Blackrock Mountain.
Arrival of the Draenei

The draenei crash-land on Draenor in the Genedar and create the Council of Exarchs.

The draenei establish Shattrath City in the location where Goria once stood.

Auchindoun and the Auchenai are established after it is discovered that the remains of the naaru D'ore are attracting the souls of deceased draenei.

The Temple of Karabor is founded. The Shadowmoon orcs begin to worship the darkened naaru K'ara as a deity, calling it the "Dark Star", but quickly outlaw the practice after discovering that wielding the Dark Star's power causes insanity.

The naaru K'ure begins attracting the souls of deceased orcs to the wreckage of the Genedar. Orcish shaman begin making pilgrimages to the site to commune with their ancestors, naming the crystal mountain "Oshu'gun".

A group of orcish exiles dwelling below Nagrand begin tapping into the Void energies bleeding from K'ure. This allows them to use shadow magic but also turns their skin a sickly white, causing the exiles to begin calling themselves "the Pale".
Draenei impact on the Orcs
Rebellion of the Goblins
The goblins of Kezan, granted heightened intelligence by the kaja'mite ore, break free of their slavery under the Zandalari and establish various cartels.

Imperator Hok'lon leads the Gorian Empire in an attempt to retake the ruins of Goria from the draenei. The attack is easily repelled by the draenei and Hok'lon is killed. The ogres flee after Velen appears on Shattrath's ramparts, wreathed in light, and tells them that they will be allowed to leave unharmed.
Ogre attack on Shattrath
The orc clans debate over how to respond to the draenei. The Bladewind clan begin raiding draenei caravans, but the attacks gradually cease when the draenei send Vindicators to guard the caravans.
Rise of tensions between Orcs and Draenei
The Expedition to Kel'Theril

A small group of high elves leave Quel'Thalas and travel to Winterspring in search of the mysteries of Kel'Theril, but end up discovering shards of the shattered Crystal of Zin-Malor. 
The expedition leader, Archmage Maenius, is corrupted by the shards and drives the elves to madness.
The Gnoll War
King Barathen Wrynn of Stormwind defeats Garfang and his gnoll armies in the Gnoll War.
Birth of Medivh

Aegwynn chose Nielas Aran to conceive a child to be her successor.
She hides the power of the Guardian of Tirisfal inside him, to be activated when he reaches maturity but Sargeras' spirit, which was hiding inside Aegwynn, possesses the infant.

Aegwynn gives birth to her first and only child, Medivh.
The Shadow Pact

Searching a way to weaken the defensers of Azeroth, Kil'jaeden find the world of Dreanor where the long fleeing Eredars renamed Draenei settled in.

Kil'jaeden, seeking to corrupt the orcs to serve the Burning Legion, contacts Gul'dan whohave been exiled from his clan and rejected by the elements.

Gul'dan is promised with untold power in exchange for agreeing to help the Burning Legion manipulate the orcs against the draenei. Gul'dan accepts, becoming the first orcish warlock.
On the eve of his fourteenth birthday, Medivh's dormant powers awake and lash out, killing his father Nielas. Medivh lies dormant for many years after this, tended to by clerics at Northshire Abbey.
Awakening of Medivh's power
Birth of Grommash Hellscream
Grommash Hellscream is born
Awakening of Medivh
Medivh awoke after a decade under a facade of control and assured the clerics and the court that he was fine.
The Gurubashi War

The Gurubashi trolls begin launching raids on human settlements in retaliation for the humans pushing farther and farther south into Gurubashi territory. King Barathen dispatches soldiers to intercept raiding parties but forbids them from striking into Gurubashi lands.

After a gruesome attack on three Westfall towns by the Gurubashi, Medivh and his two friends Anduin Lothar and Prince Llane Wrynn sneak into Stranglethorn to assassinate the Gurubashi leader, Jok'non. They succeed, but only after Medivh unleashes his full might as a Guardian.

The Gurubashi rally under Jok'non's son, Zan'non, and march to war against Stormwind, launching an attack on Stormwind City itself. Barathen dies during the battle and Llane is forced to convince Medivh to unleash his full Guardian powers to repel the attack. Llane, Medivh and Anduin are hailed as heroes by the kingdom.
Aegwynn confronts Medivh

Medivh is confronted by his mother Aegwynn at Karazhan. She urges him to isolate himself from the world and leaves him with a caretaker, Moroes.

The Council of Tirisfal discover Medivh and begin sending apprentices to study under him, but none last for longer than a day.

Moroes notices Medivh's ever-darkening mood and convinces him to begin launching banquets and feasts to lift his spirits.

Two young orcs, Orgrim Doomhammer and Durotan, are saved from an ogre by a group of draenei. 
The draenei invite them to the nearby settlement of Telmor, where Velen requests an audience with them before the two orcs are escorted back to the borders of Gorgrond.
Young Durotan and Orgrim meet Velen
Talgath, a high ranking leader of the Burning Legion, discovers the draenei civilization on Draenor. Kil'jaeden commands him to observe the inhabitants of the world for the time being.
Discovery of Draenor by the Burning Legion
The Battle of Bladespire

Final and most important battle of the conflict between the Bladespire ogres and the Frostwolf and Whiteclaw orc clans.

It led to the liberation of the mok'nathal half-breeds from their brutal Bladespire masters.

Ga'nar's, Durotan brother, dies during the battle and although Durotan remained to carry on the family line, Garad, chieftain of the Frostwolves clan, never recovered from losing his second son.

Gul'dan inundates the Throne of the Elements with fel magic, throwing the elements into disarray across the world, and also uses his magic to create the worst outbreak of the red pox in orcish history. 

Many orcs contract the plague at the Kosh'harg festival. Under the leadership of the Frostwolf chieftain Garad, the plague bearers establish a village in Nagrand to quarantine the afflicted. 

The village is named Garadar in Garad's honor after he succumbs to the pox.

Medivh continues to study demonic lore and Azerothian history and becomes convinced that the world is inherently flawed, too divided by petty rivalries to ever unite into a single force in case of a demonic invasion. 

He concludes that he needs an army to change things and begins venturing out into the cosmos, eventually discovering Draenor and the orcs.
Medivh discovers Dreanor

Gul'dan returns to his home village and burns it and everyone within it to ash to prevent anyone from learning about his past.

He then ventures to the Shadowmoon clan and convinces them to let him join them, claiming that his home village was destroyed by ogres. 

Gul'dan wins the friendship of the Shadowmoon chieftain, the shaman Ner'zhul, allowing Kil'jaeden to begin manipulating Ner'zhul's thoughts.

Gul'dan manipulates the Bladewind clan into launching raids on draenei caravans, killing and kidnapping dozens of draenei. Vindicator Maraad and the draenei retaliate and storm the Bladewind village, but when Maraad sees the corpse of his sister Leran he goes into a rampage across the village. 

Gul'dan kills the few surviving Bladewinds as they attempt to flee. He then returns to the Shadowmoon and tells of how the draenei launched an unprovoked massacre against the Bladewinds. 

Meanwhile, Kil'jaeden appears to Ner'zhul in his dreams, disguised as the spirit of his deceased mate Rulkan, and tells him that the draenei are planning to destroy the orcs. Ner'zhul calls for a clan meeting at Oshu'gun, where the orc chieftains agree to band together to defeat the draenei, marking the creation of the Horde.
Gul'dan plots for war

The orcs begin launching sporadic attacks against draenei hunting parties. 
The draenei, assuming that the orcs have simply been agitated by the elemental turmoil, begin organizing and constructing new defenses.

Ner'zhul's apprehension about the war with the draenei grows. 
Kil'jaeden appears to him in the form of Rulkan and tells him of powerful beings who could aid the orcs, and the night after Kil'jaeden appears again as a radiant elemental entity and urges him to push the Horde to victory and exterminate the draenei. 

Ner'zhul secretly embarks on a journey to Oshu'gun to seek the guidance of the ancestors, but Kil'jaeden is aware of his plans and tells Gul'dan to gather allies to control the Shadowmoon, since Ner'zhul can no longer be relied upon. Gul'dan recruits Teron'gor and several other shaman and begin teaching them fel magic.

At Oshu'gun, the real Rulkan and the other ancestors tell Ner'zhul that he was being manipulated by Kil'jaeden and condemn the shaman for having been used by the demon lord. 

Ner'zhul falls into despair and is captured by Gul'dan's followers, who treat him as little more than a slave.
Ner'zhul's fall

Displeased by the disarray and infighting in the Horde, Kil'jaeden commands Gul'dan to find a single, true leader for the orcs — a warchief. 
Gul'dan convinces Blackhand to take up the position after training some of the Blackrock clan's shaman how to wield fel magic and magically age young orcs, including Blackhand's young sons, Dal'rend and Maim.

Gul'dan forms the Shadow Council to watch over the orcs and includes Blackhand in the organization, but Gul'dan's trusted Shadowmoon warlocks secretly form the inner circle of the organization. 
The warlock recruits new members for the council, including Cho'gall and Garona, and creates a group called the necrolytes.

Zagrel, Chieftain of the Whiteclaw clan, is assassinated by Garona on behalf of Gul'dan for speaking out against the Horde.
Tensions in the Horde

At a clan meeting at Oshu'gun, Gul'dan persuades many shaman into becoming warlocks and convinces the clan chieftains to unanimously vote for Blackhand as their warchief.

Blackhand orders the construction of the Citadel, later known as Hellfire Citadel, and organizes the various clans into specific roles within the Horde. He also forms a new clan known as the Black Tooth Grin and names Eitrigg, Orgrim Doomhammer and Varok Saurfang as his lieutenants in the Blackrock clan.

Blackhand sends warlocks to magically age the adolescents of other clans. The orcs' skin begins to turn a sickly green.

Cho'gall recruits the pale orcs into the Horde and forms the Twilight's Hammer clan.
Blackhand is declared Warchief
The fall of the Draenei

The draenei's morale begins to founder as the orcs launch coordinated assaults on minor settlements and outposts across the dying world. Velen and the exarchs, knowing that their only chance of survival is to hold off the onslaught and hope that the Burning Legion does not launch a full-scale invasion, order their forces to withdraw to Shattrath and Karabor. 

The elemental spirits pool their power into the mighty Firelord, Cyrukh, to stop the desecration of the land.

The orcs gather for an assault on Karabor. Cyrukh appears in a nearby volcano to confront them, but Gul'dan and his warlocks gather on the volcano's slopes to shatter the being's physical form and infuse its power into the orcs, shattering the last connection between the orcs and the elements. The volcano becomes known as the Hand of Gul'dan.

The draenei hold the orcish assault at bay for a time but are defeated when the Horde uses the power of the Dark Star to kill or drive insane many of the defenders and permanently darken Karabor, turning it into the Black Temple. Velen and the survivors manage to flee via the harbor.
The corruption of the Horde

The orcs gather at a mountain near the Citadel and drink the blood of Mannoroth at Gul'dan's urging. Durotan forbids the Frostwolves from drinking after having received an anonymous message from Ner'zhul, while Orgrim refuses out of suspicion for the growing corruption of the orcs and Draenor. 
Those who do drink the blood are driven into a ferocious bloodlust and march against Shattrath as Gul'dan infuses the mountain with fel energy, transforming it into the Throne of Kil'jaeden.

The victims of the red pox quarantined in Garadar remain isolated from the fel corruption, leading them to become known as the Mag'har, "Uncorrupted".

Velen leads many Shattrath civilians to a refuge in Telredor. The orcs launch an assault on Shattrath, unleashing the red mist against the draenei. Before long, the city falls to the Horde.

Many of the survivors retreat to Auchindoun. Teron'gor and other Shadow Council agents are dispatched to the mausoleum, but when they are repelled by the draenei and Auchindoun's spirits they attempt to summon a powerful demon to aid them. 
Instead, they accidentally summon Murmur, whose arrival blasts Auchindoun apart and levels the surrounding forests. The warlocks bind Murmur within Auchindoun to prevent it from wreaking havoc on the Horde.
The March of the Horde

More draenei survivors arrive at Telredor. The ones afflicted by the red mist mutate into Broken, and the populace of Telredor exile them into the wilds out of fear that the condition might spread. Some Broken continue to degrade into Lost Ones.

Blackhand turns his attention on Draenor's other inhabitants. Kilrogg Deadeye and the Bleeding Hollow clan launch a campaign against Farahlon, while Grommash Hellscream and Cho'gall topple Highmaul. Elsewhere, the Frostwolf, Whiteclaw and Thunderlord clans are charged with hunting down the ogres, ogron, gronn and magnaron, though only the Thunderlords obey.

Kargath Bladefist leads a force to conquer the arakkoa capital, Skyreach. 
The orcs ally with the Outcast arakkoa, who agree to infiltrate Skyreach and sabotage the high arakkoa's superweapon. Kargath and his forces then slaughter high and cursed arakkoa alike, casting some of the former into Sethekk Hollow. 
These cursed high arakkoa rally under Grizzik, who leads his people to take refuge in Auchindoun.

Kil'jaeden ceases to communicate with Gul'dan on Sargeras' orders. The orcs begin to flounder on Draenor as the world slowly dies. 

The threat of starvation causes the orcs to hunt many of Draenor's native creatures to extinction and begin fighting amongst themselves.
Medivh appears to Gul'dan and the Shadow Council and tells them of Azeroth, as well as showing a vision of the Tomb of Sargeras to Gul'dan. The construction of the Dark Portal begins.
Medivh contacts Gul'dan

Created in a joint effort between Gul'dan and the demonically possessed Medivh, the Dark Portal is opened.

The gateway between the worlds of Azeroth and Draenor allow the Horde to invade Azeroth thus beginning the First War.

Arrival of the Horde through the Dark Portal
The orcish Horde emerges on Azeroth through the Dark Portal and begins the First War against Stormwind. Blackhand leads the invasion as the Horde establishes its foothold in the kingdom.
Khadgar Becomes Medivh's Apprentice
The young mage Khadgar is sent to study under Medivh in Karazhan. His apprenticeship places him near the Guardian just as the First War begins to unfold.
Banishment of the Frostwolves
Durotan and the Frostwolf clan are cast out from the Horde after challenging Gul'dan's corruption. The exile leaves the Frostwolves isolated but preserves their honor.
Birth of Thrall / Death of Durotan and Draka
Thrall is born to Durotan and Draka shortly before both parents are murdered. Their deaths leave the infant to grow up in captivity, setting the stage for the Horde's future.
Death of Medivh / Orgrim Kills Blackhand
Khadgar, Garona, and their allies bring down Medivh to stop the Guardian's corruption. During the same turning point in the war, Orgrim Doomhammer slays Blackhand and seizes command of the Horde.
Fall of Stormwind / Assassination of King Llane
Stormwind falls to the Horde after Garona assassinates King Llane Wrynn. Survivors flee north, carrying news of the war to the rest of the human kingdoms.
Khadgar
A gifted human mage who becomes Medivh's apprentice and later one of Azeroth's foremost defenders against the Horde and the Burning Legion.
Medivh
The last Guardian of Tirisfal, possessed by Sargeras and manipulated into opening the Dark Portal to Azeroth.
Garona Halforcen
A half-orc assassin used by the Horde and the Shadow Council, remembered above all for killing King Llane during the fall of Stormwind.
Durotan
Chieftain of the Frostwolf clan who resists Gul'dan's corruption and is later murdered after being exiled from the Horde.
Draka
Mate of Durotan and mother of Thrall, killed alongside Durotan shortly after their son's birth.
Thrall
Born during the First War, Thrall survives the murder of his parents and will eventually rise to remake the Horde.
Orgrim Doomhammer
A legendary orc warrior who kills Blackhand and becomes Warchief of the Horde during the First War.
Blackhand
The first Warchief of the Horde on Azeroth, ruled largely as a puppet of Gul'dan before being slain by Orgrim Doomhammer.
Llane Wrynn
King of Stormwind during the First War, assassinated by Garona as the kingdom falls to the Horde.
Horde
The orcish Horde that invades Azeroth through the Dark Portal and wages the First and Second Wars.
Stormwind
The human kingdom that first faces the Horde's invasion when the Dark Portal opens.
Frostwolf Clan
The clan led by Durotan, exiled from the Horde after opposing Gul'dan's schemes.
Shadow Council
Gul'dan's secret cabal of warlocks, which manipulates the Horde from behind the scenes during the First War.
Formation of the Council of Seven Nations
Following the fall of Stormwind, the human kingdoms gather to coordinate their response to the Horde. Anduin Lothar helps rally the northern powers into a common front.
Formation of the Alliance of Lordaeron
The kingdoms of humanity and their allies formally unite under the Alliance of Lordaeron to oppose the Horde during the Second War.
Founding of the Order of the Silver Hand
Uther Lightbringer and the clergy of Lordaeron found the Order of the Silver Hand, creating Azeroth's first paladin order to strengthen the Alliance.
Alexstrasza Captured at Grim Batol
The Dragonmaw clan enslaves Alexstrasza at Grim Batol, using the Demon Soul to bind the Life-Binder and weaponize the red dragonflight.
Gul'dan Creates the First Death Knights
Gul'dan pioneers necromantic warfare by creating the first death knights, binding orcish spirits to fallen human bodies in service of the Horde.
Battle of Hillsbrad
Horde and Alliance forces clash in Hillsbrad as the war spreads across Lordaeron. Zul'jin and the Amani become key allies of the Horde in the campaign.
Siege of Lordaeron / Gul'dan's Betrayal
The Horde presses its assault into the heart of Lordaeron, but Gul'dan abandons Orgrim's campaign in pursuit of his own ambitions, weakening the Horde at a decisive moment.
Death of Anduin Lothar at Blackrock Spire
Anduin Lothar falls in battle against Orgrim Doomhammer at Blackrock Spire, becoming one of the defining martyrs of the Alliance.
Khadgar Destroys the Dark Portal
Khadgar destroys the Dark Portal at the end of the Second War, severing the Horde's main path between Azeroth and Draenor.
Ner'zhul Reopens the Portal / Draenor Shatters
Ner'zhul tears open multiple portals in a desperate bid for escape and power. The magical catastrophe breaks Draenor apart, leaving behind the shattered world of Outland.
Ner'zhul Becomes the Lich King
Kil'jaeden captures Ner'zhul and binds his spirit into the Frozen Throne, creating the first Lich King as an instrument of the Burning Legion.
Anduin Lothar
Champion of Stormwind and supreme commander of the Alliance during the Second War, remembered as the Lion of Azeroth.
Uther Lightbringer
One of the first paladins and founder of the Order of the Silver Hand, Uther becomes a central hero of the Alliance.
Gul'dan
The most infamous orc warlock, founder of the Shadow Council, and architect of many of the Horde's darkest acts.
Alexstrasza
The red Dragon Aspect of Life, enslaved by the Dragonmaw clan during the Second War before later being freed.
Deathwing
Formerly Neltharion the Earth-Warder, Deathwing manipulates the war from the shadows and helps enable Alexstrasza's capture.
Terenas Menethil II
King of Lordaeron and one of the principal leaders behind the formation of the Alliance of Lordaeron.
Zul'jin
Warlord of the Amani trolls who allies with the Horde against the Alliance during the Second War.
Ner'zhul
Former elder shaman of the Shadowmoon clan who later shatters Draenor and is transformed into the Lich King.
Alliance of Lordaeron
The grand wartime coalition of human kingdoms and allies formed to resist the Horde during the Second War.
Seven Kingdoms
The major human kingdoms of Azeroth whose rulers and armies provide the backbone of the Alliance response to the Horde.
Order of the Silver Hand
The first paladin order, founded in Lordaeron to combine martial strength with the Light against the Horde.
Dragonmaw Clan
An orc clan that captures and enslaves Alexstrasza, forcing the red dragonflight into service of the Horde.
Death Knights
Necromantic warriors created by Gul'dan, representing one of the earliest undead weapons fielded by the Horde.
Amani
The forest troll empire of northern Lordaeron, led in war by Zul'jin and aligned with the Horde during the Second War.
Horde Remnants
The surviving fragments of the Horde after its defeat, scattered and diminished but still dangerous under leaders like Ner'zhul.
Burning Legion
Sargeras' demonic army, which continues to manipulate orcish leaders and ultimately reshapes Ner'zhul into the Lich King.
The Scourge Spreads Through Lordaeron
Undeath begins to spread openly across Lordaeron as Kel'Thuzad and the Lich King's agents prepare the kingdom for the Third War.
Culling of Stratholme
Arthas orders the purge of Stratholme to stop its citizens from becoming undead, a ruthless decision that marks his moral collapse.
Arthas Claims Frostmourne
In Northrend, Arthas takes up Frostmourne despite its curse, sacrificing his soul for the power to defeat Mal'Ganis.
Arthas Murders King Terenas
Upon returning to Lordaeron as a death knight, Arthas kills his father Terenas and delivers the kingdom to the Scourge.
Invasion of Quel'Thalas and the Sunwell's Corruption
Arthas invades Quel'Thalas, slays Sylvanas, and uses the Sunwell to resurrect Kel'Thuzad, forever scarring the high elven kingdom.
Battle of Mount Hyjal
Alliance, Horde, and Night Elves unite at Hyjal to resist Archimonde and the Legion, ending the Third War with a desperate victory.
Illidan Attempts to Destroy the Frozen Throne
Empowered by the Legion, Illidan tries to shatter the Frozen Throne from afar but fails, deepening his rivalry with Arthas and Ner'zhul.
Kael'thas and the Blood Elves Join Illidan
Kael'thas leads the blood elves into Illidan's service, seeking survival and power in the wake of Quel'Thalas's devastation.
Founding of Durotar and Orgrimmar
Thrall leads the Horde to Kalimdor and establishes Durotar and Orgrimmar, creating a new homeland after the chaos of the Third War.
The Forsaken Join the Horde
Sylvanas secures the Forsaken a place within the Horde, forging a pragmatic alliance that reshapes Azeroth's political landscape.
Arthas Menethil
Prince of Lordaeron who falls to darkness during the Third War and becomes the Lich King's greatest champion.
Jaina Proudmoore
Powerful archmage and leader of the human survivors who helps guide the Alliance through the Third War and its aftermath.
Sylvanas Windrunner
Ranger-General of Silvermoon, slain by Arthas and later reborn as the Banshee Queen and leader of the Forsaken.
Kel'Thuzad
Former mage of Dalaran turned lich, one of the chief architects of the Scourge's invasion of Lordaeron.
Mal'Ganis
A dreadlord of the Burning Legion who lures Arthas into the brutal decisions that ultimately doom him.
Illidan Stormrage
Night elf sorcerer and demon hunter whose pursuit of power places him at the center of Azeroth's struggle against the Legion and the Lich King.
Kael'thas Sunstrider
Prince of Quel'Thalas who leads the blood elves after their kingdom's fall and later allies with Illidan.
Rexxar
Champion of the Horde who aids Thrall in securing Durotar and defending the young nation in Kalimdor.
Archimonde
One of the Burning Legion's greatest commanders, destroyed at Mount Hyjal when Azeroth's defenders make their final stand.
Scourge
The undead army of the Lich King, responsible for the fall of Lordaeron and much of the devastation of the Third War.
Quel'Thalas
The high elven kingdom laid waste by Arthas during the Third War, a tragedy that gives rise to the blood elves.
Alliance
The broader coalition of Azeroth's peoples that survives the collapse of Lordaeron and continues the struggle against the Legion and the Scourge.
Night Elves
Ancient defenders of Kalimdor whose armies and druids become decisive at Mount Hyjal.
Illidari
Followers and allies of Illidan Stormrage, gathered in defiance of both the Legion and more conventional powers.
Blood Elves
The surviving high elves of Quel'Thalas, renamed in memory of the fallen and led by Kael'thas after the kingdom's ruin.
Forsaken
Undead freed from the Lich King's direct control under Sylvanas, who found a place for their people within the Horde.
Battle of Grim Batol / Liberation of Alexstrasza
Rhonin, Vereesa, Korialstrasz, and their allies break the Dragonmaw clan's hold over Alexstrasza, restoring the Life-Binder to freedom.
War of the Spider
The Lich King wages war beneath Northrend against the nerubian empire, breaking one of the greatest underground powers of Azeroth.
World of Warcraft Classic Campaign
In the wake of the Third War, Azeroth enters the age of World of Warcraft. Old threats re-emerge, local conflicts intensify, and the rivalry between Alliance and Horde grows sharper.
Ragefire Chasm and the Shadow Council in Orgrimmar
Cultists and infiltrators tied to the Shadow Council undermine Orgrimmar from the depths of Ragefire Chasm, forcing the Horde to root them out from within its own capital.
Blackrock Depths / Moira Bronzebeard Kidnapped
Dagran Thaurissan's hold over Blackrock Depths and his union with Moira Bronzebeard deepen the Dark Iron crisis beneath Blackrock Mountain.
Stratholme / Baron Rivendare and the Scarlet Crusade
The ruined city of Stratholme remains a battleground of undeath, fanaticism, and survival, where Baron Rivendare and the Scarlet Crusade embody two different corruptions.
Naxxramas and the Scourge Invasion
Kel'Thuzad's necropolis Naxxramas looms over Azeroth as the Scourge launches a new wave of terror during the final phase of Classic.
Blackwing Lair and Nefarian's Defeat
Deep within Blackwing Lair, Nefarian advances twisted draconic experiments until adventurers finally bring down one of Deathwing's greatest heirs.
Zul'Gurub and the Return of Hakkar
Hakkar the Soulflayer manifests again in Zul'Gurub, threatening Stranglethorn with blood magic and ancient troll power.
War of Ahn'Qiraj / Awakening of C'Thun
The gates of Ahn'Qiraj are opened and the armies of Azeroth unite in a massive war against the qiraji and the Old God C'Thun.
End of Classic / Rising Alliance-Horde Tensions
As Classic draws to a close, the greatest threats are contained but the underlying rivalry between Alliance and Horde grows stronger, setting the stage for Outland.
Korialstrasz
Consort of Alexstrasza, known in mortal guise as Krasus, and a key actor in the effort to free the red Dragon Aspect from Grim Batol.
Rhonin
A mage whose daring mission to Grim Batol becomes central to the liberation of Alexstrasza and the fate of the dragonflights.
Vereesa Windrunner
High elf ranger and sister of Sylvanas, who joins Rhonin's mission and later becomes a key Alliance-aligned hero.
The Lich King
The frozen ruler of the undead, first born from Ner'zhul and later united with Arthas Menethil.
Dagran Thaurissan
Emperor of the Dark Iron dwarves in Blackrock Depths, whose rule binds the Dark Irons tightly to Blackrock Mountain.
Moira Bronzebeard
Daughter of Magni Bronzebeard, drawn into the politics of the Dark Iron dwarves deep beneath Blackrock Mountain.
Baron Rivendare
A death knight who rules over part of ruined Stratholme and serves as one of the Scourge's most infamous commanders in Classic.
Nefarian
Son of Deathwing and lord of Blackwing Lair, obsessed with breeding powerful chromatic dragons.
Hakkar
The Soulflayer, a blood god worshipped by troll cultists and unleashed again in Zul'Gurub.
C'Thun
An Old God imprisoned beneath Ahn'Qiraj whose awakening ignites one of the largest wars of the Classic era.
Red Dragonflight
The dragonflight of life led by Alexstrasza, victimized by the Dragonmaw clan and later restored to freedom.
Nerubians
The spider empire of Northrend that resists the Lich King in the War of the Spider before being crushed.
Old Gods
Ancient void entities buried within Azeroth, whose influence resurges throughout the Classic era.
Dark Iron Dwarves
The dwarven clan ruling beneath Blackrock Mountain, long entangled with fire, tyranny, and elemental power.
Scarlet Crusade
A fanatical order dedicated to destroying undeath, but consumed by zealotry and corruption during the Classic era.
Black Dragonflight
The dragonflight corrupted by Deathwing, whose schemes continue through Blackrock Mountain and Blackwing Lair.
Gurubashi Empire
The ancient troll empire of Stranglethorn, whose ruins become the stage for Hakkar's return in Zul'Gurub.
Black Empire
The old world-spanning dominion of the Old Gods, briefly echoed again when Ahn'Qiraj stirs and C'Thun awakens.
Reopening of the Dark Portal / Arrival in Outland
The Dark Portal is reopened from Azeroth, and Alliance and Horde forces step into shattered Outland to confront old and new threats.
Alliance and Horde Expedition in Outland
Campaigns across Hellfire Peninsula, Zangarmarsh, and beyond draw Azeroth's armies into conflict alongside the Sha'tar, Aldor, and Scryers.
Fall of Magtheridon and Illidan's Rule
Magtheridon is overthrown as Illidan consolidates his power in Outland, with Akama and his allies maneuvering against him from within.
Tempest Keep Campaign and Kael'thas Betrayal
Kael'thas turns from the outland struggle to serve the Legion's wider goals, while the Tempest Keep conflict reshapes blood elf destiny.
Sunwell Crisis and Defeat of Kil'jaeden
At the Sunwell, Azeroth's champions and blood elf defenders stop Kil'jaeden's return and close the Burning Crusade era with a decisive victory.
Northrend Campaign Begins
Alliance and Horde launch their northern war against the Scourge, while Tirion and the Argent Crusade prepare a united front against the Lich King.
Battle of the Wrathgate and the Undercity Crisis
The Wrathgate disaster shocks both factions, and the subsequent struggle for Undercity exposes deep fractures in Azeroth's uneasy alliances.
Ulduar and the Fall of Yogg-Saron
In ancient Ulduar, Brann and Azeroth's champions uncover titan mysteries and shatter Yogg-Saron's influence before it can consume the north.
Argent Tournament and the Ebon Blade Offensive
The Argent Tournament forges a united assault force while Darion's Ebon Blade wages relentless war against Icecrown's outer defenses.
Assault on Icecrown Citadel / Fall of the Lich King
The final assault breaches Icecrown Citadel; the Lich King falls, and Bolvar takes the frozen crown to contain the Scourge.
Velen
Prophet-leader of the draenei, who guides his people from Outland toward a renewed alliance with Azeroth's defenders.
Akama
Broken leader of the Ashtongue, central to the struggle against Illidan's rule in Shadowmoon Valley and the Black Temple.
Lady Liadrin
Blood elf commander of the Blood Knights, active in the defense and restoration of Quel'Thalas during the Sunwell crisis.
A'dal
A naaru of Shattrath and one of the principal leaders of the Sha'tar coalition in Outland.
Kil'jaeden
Demon lord of the Burning Legion whose attempted return through the Sunwell marks the final crisis of the Burning Crusade.
Bolvar Fordragon
Alliance commander at Wrathgate who ultimately becomes the new jailer of the damned by taking up the Lich King's burden.
Darion Mograine
Leader of the Knights of the Ebon Blade and a major figure in the campaign to break the Scourge's hold over Northrend.
Tirion Fordring
Highlord of the Argent Crusade who unites Azeroth's champions for the final war against the Lich King.
Brann Bronzebeard
Explorer and loremaster whose discoveries in Northrend and Ulduar reveal critical titan history.
Yogg-Saron
An Old God imprisoned beneath Ulduar, whose whispers and corruption threaten all of Northrend.
Draenei of the Exodar
The surviving draenei who reach Azeroth aboard the Exodar and become a core Alliance people during the Outland era.
The Sha'tar
Naaru-led coalition based in Shattrath, coordinating resistance against demonic and tyrannical forces in Outland.
Aldor
Priestly military order aligned with the Sha'tar, and one of Shattrath's two major political-religious blocs.
Scryers
Blood elf magisters in Shattrath whose arcane expertise and rivalry with the Aldor shape Outland diplomacy.
Argent Crusade
Order founded to unite anti-Scourge forces in Northrend under a single righteous command.
Knights of the Ebon Blade
Former death knights who rebelled against the Lich King and became a key strike force against Icecrown.
Titan-forged of Ulduar
The keepers and constructs of Ulduar, central to the war against Yogg-Saron and the safeguarding of titan secrets.
The Shattering / Return of Deathwing
Deathwing erupts from Deepholm, shattering Azeroth's lands and seas and plunging the world into the Cataclysm.
Worgen and Goblins Enter the Faction War
Gilnean worgen join the Alliance while Bilgewater goblins rally to the Horde, intensifying global faction conflict.
Twilight's Hammer Uprising
Cho'gall's cult spreads chaos across Azeroth as the Earthen Ring and both factions struggle to stabilize a world in upheaval.
Firelands Campaign / Fall of Ragnaros
The campaign into the Firelands ends with Ragnaros defeated on his own plane, reducing one of the greatest elemental threats.
Dragon Soul / Deathwing's Defeat
Thrall and the united dragonflights wield the Dragon Soul to defeat Deathwing and end the Cataclysm's central threat.
Varian Wrynn
King of Stormwind and a defining Alliance war leader during the Cataclysm era.
Garrosh Hellscream
Warchief of the Horde during Cataclysm, whose militaristic policies reshape faction warfare.
Cho'gall
Two-headed ogre leader of the Twilight's Hammer and a major architect of Old God-aligned chaos.
Ragnaros
The Firelord, who returns in Cataclysm and is confronted directly in the Firelands.
Nozdormu
Aspect of Time, central to the Dragon Soul campaign and the defense of Azeroth's timeline.
Twilight's Hammer
Doomsday cult serving the Old Gods, active across Cataclysm's major crisis zones.
Earthen Ring
Shamanic order led by Thrall in the effort to heal Azeroth's wounded elements during Cataclysm.
Dragon Aspects United
The combined strength of Azeroth's dragon aspects brought together for the Dragon Soul offensive.
Elemental Lords
Primal rulers of elemental planes, whose upheaval and wars fuel much of the Cataclysm conflict.
